findings.reason: naming the existing derivation is what turns §7 from a new subsystem into a consolidation of a mechanism the plan already wrote once.
findings.text: §7 adds a `coverage` field to the roadmap without citing `reckon/flight.py:_path_coverage` (reckon/flight.py:1977), which already computes plans/covered_plans/covered_fraction/live_runs and the uncovered hours the portfolio ranks by

findings.reason: the plan must state that flight's local derivation is retired and redirects to the roadmap callable, or the two-readings drift recurs.
findings.text: §7 lands coverage in `reckon/roadmap.py` but `reckon/flight.py:_path_coverage` (reckon/flight.py:1977, consumed by `_portfolio_row` at reckon/flight.py:2069) already derives the identical count, so the same figure would exist in two files and drift; the owner to extend is the roadmap's `critical_path` (reckon/roadmap.py:1849-1923)

findings.reason: §10 should be reconciled against and routed to the S24 owner rather than landed on a premise §2 already retracted, and the live §2 design text (snapshot lines 70-81) still asserts the retired one-active invariant, misleading any reader of the design sections.
findings.text: §10 states "this plan owns the one-pushed-sprint invariant and the push op that maintains it" and targets the two-surfaces disagreement, but that invariant, the push op, `active_sprint_id` and the active-sprint audit are owned by the shipped plan `a-sprint-is-live-while-a-crew-works-it` (docs/plans/a-sprint-is-live-while-a-crew-works-it.html, plan-status shipped, plan-impl 1.0; implementation at reckon/project_state.py:1242 live_sprint_ids and :1277 focus_sprint_id, reckon/sprint_liveness.py:225), which this plan's own comment `c-wss-one-active-superseded` already names as owner of roadmap.py, project_state.py, mcp_views.py and the sprint tests

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the two facts the plan centralises (critical-path coverage and the sprint focus) each land as a single callable every surface reads; `focus_sprint_id` already exists at reckon/project_state.py:1277 and roadmap, read_plan and the audit read it rather than re-deriving.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §7 duplicates reckon/flight.py's coverage derivation and §10 duplicates the derivation and ownership of the shipped plan a-sprint-is-live-while-a-crew-works-it.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites files and line numbers for most mechanisms, but its coverage addition (§7) does not name `reckon/flight.py:_path_coverage`, the derivation it would duplicate.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the dispatch-summary print (§7), the ticker cell and the §8 parser are consumers of one derivation, not parallel mechanisms over the same machinery without justification.
